summary: Initial compliance-focused discovery. SE agreed to run region-locked bench and propose options.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-17
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Ortega (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Elena Kovács (Sterling, Head of Platform); Markus Heller (Sterling, Security Lead); Priya Reddy (Sterling, Legal Counsel); Jonah Lee (Sterling, Infra)

Summary: short intake, lots of compliance Qs — logging redaction and residency prioritized.

00:00 - Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? I got Jasmine and Ravi from Redwood. you all good on our end?
00:07 - Elena: Yep hi, Elena here.
00:09 - Markus: Markus present.
00:11 - Priya: Priya here.
00:13 - Jonah: Jonah
00:16 - Jasmine: Great. The aim here is to understand your residency and compliance constraints so we can propose Hosted, Dedicated or Private. feel free to jump in.
00:28 - Elena: High level — we're a European asset manager, we can't have customer PII or KYC details leave EU, and logs are tied to client accounts. Senior compliance wants proof that logs don't get replicated outside region. Also we have some funds handling small health-data ad hoc events — so HIPAA-like controls apply.
00:48 - Ravi: Understood. We can do region-locked hosting, and private control plane —our private option runs inside customer VPC and can be on-prem. question: is the requirement purely residency or also that encryption keys must stay in EU?
01:05 - Markus: Keys must stay in EU and be under our KMS, ideally HSM-backed. we cannot hand over key material to subs unless it's contractually limited.
01:16 - Jasmine: So two levers: where data sits and who controls KMS. Hosted can do region-locking but if you require customer-managed keys we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives reserved capacity in region with KMS integration, Private gives full control. (slight pause) sorry slight mis-said — Dedicated can integrate with cust KMS depending on network setup.
01:40 - Priya: On logging — we have a long list: request metadata, prompts, response token traces for debugging, but compliance says we cannot keep certain fields (PII) in logs beyond 7 days and some fields must be redacted at ingest. can Redwood support field-level redaction and configurable retention windows per tenant?
02:01 - Ravi: short answer yes. we have a log pipeline where you can enable auto-redact on certain patterns, and retention is policy driven per-tenant. caveat: current hosted pipeline stores some traces in aggregated form for quality-monitoring — we can show how that's pseudonymized. also transcription: our auto redact has false positives/negatives sometimes.
02:20 - Elena: We need guarantees — legal will want to see proof that redaction is applied before logs leave the VPC for hosted.
02:28 - Jasmine: Right — for hosted we can provide architecture diagrams and data flow with the redaction step called out. for Dedicated/Private the redaction step can be in your VPC so logs never cross your boundary.
02:39 - Jonah: technical: do you store KV cache or prefixes that could leak prompts on disk? we have concerns about KV cache persistence and snapshot backups.
02:47 - Ravi: yes we use KV cache at runtime to accelerate seq generation; in hosted variants we maintain cache nodes but we can configure in-memory only (no disk snapshot) for sensitive workloads. for Dedicated we can set ephemeral caches, and for Private it's under your infra policy. backups: hosted backups are encrypted and region-scoped but if your policy forbids any disk persistence we can adapt.
03:12 - Markus: Regarding audits — SOC 2 is required, ISO 27001 preferred, and we need audit logs with immutability for queries. also access controls: SSO with SAML, SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC. how mature is Redwood here?
03:27 - Jasmine: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, SAML and SCIM, RBAC with per-route permissions. we can provide evidence and our compliance pack. small note — sometimes the doc references the 'control plane' as ctrl-plane in our docs which gets mis-printed.
03:44 - Priya: subprocessors — do you use any third party for evaluation or QA that might access logs? auditors ask about subprocessors list and any sub-sub-processors.
03:53 - Ravi: we do use a monitoring vendor for aggregated metrics; they do not receive raw prompts. we can provide a subprocessor list and propose minimization commitments in DPA.
04:05 - Elena: Another nuance — we need to know whether embeddings or model outputs are persisted and whether we can opt out of retention for certain customer classes.
04:15 - Ravi: embeddings can be cached for reuse by default but we can configure not to persist; Redwood Optimize may suggest caching to reduce cost but it's configurable.
04:26 - Jonah: Do you do any cross-region fallback that might cause data to egress during outages? like if eu capacity saturated does request go to us-east?
04:36 - Jasmine: By default we route by region, but you can enable strict region-only routing; if you allow cost/latency fallback then requests can route out-of-region. for strict compliance you'd set no-fallback.
04:47 - Markus: KMS — you mentioned we could bring our keys, how does that work with hosted? like can we put a key in our cloud KMS and have Redwood use it without key material ever leaving our KMS?
04:58 - Ravi: yes, through envelope encryption — Redwood can be configured to use customer-managed CMKs via cloud provider KMS and HSM where supported. we keep a transient working key in memory, never stored on disk. caveat: some model acceleration paths may require key-wrapping; we can detail in design doc.
05:20 - Priya: Contractually we'll push for EEA data residency clause, no subprocessing without consent, right to delete logs, and evidence for redaction. also sample incident response SLAs.
05:33 - Jasmine: Noted. We'll include these clauses in the sample contract. Any strict timeline for procurement/legal review?
05:40 - Priya: if we like the technical answers we'll aim for a pilot contract in early september, procurement needs the compliance pack before that.
05:47 - Jasmine: OK, timeline makes sense. Next — question on telemetry: we sometimes collect token-level telemetry for billing. can that be aggregated instead of saving raw tokens?
05:58 - Ravi: yes, billing telemetry is configurable; we can provide aggregated token counts per-tenant and hide content. if you need per-call billing we can provide hashed identifiers rather than raw tokens.
06:15 - Elena: For HIPAA-like data: we will have a few data streams tagged as health events; they must be treated as PHI — does Redwood sign BAA or equivalent and support HIPAA controls in Dedicated/Private?
06:28 - Jasmine: Our hosted path currently is not HIPAA-certified out-of-the-box; we offer Dedicated with contractual BAAs in certain configurations and Private where you can fully control environment for PHI. we'll flag for Legal.
06:40 - Jonah: Operational question — do you keep control plane logs separate from tenant logs? we want to be sure operator access can't join tenant-level prompts with account telemetry.
06:52 - Ravi: control plane logs are separate and access controlled; operator access is audited. in Dedicated we can enable customer-only access patterns and in Private it is within your infra boundaries.
07:05 - Markus: A subtle point — we need attestations that debug snapshots are redacted before any support engineers see them. do you have automated redaction for support snapshots?
07:14 - Ravi: yes we have redaction pipeline for snapshots and we can require that support snapshots only can be pulled with an internal ticket that states purpose; we also do manual QA but manual processes have human risk — we can add additional controls for sensitive classes.
07:29 - Priya: Ok let's talk procurement: we'll want the security pack, subprocessor list, and sample SLA. can you also include a sample data flow diagram and an explicit statement about no cross-border logs for hosted-eu if region-only enabled?
07:45 - Jasmine: Absolutely. We'll include that. any blockers from your side to continue to a bench/pilot?
07:53 - Elena: Not yet; we need the security package and the bench numbers for eu-west latency and for a private key integration proof-of-concept.
08:03 - Jasmine: Good. We'll do bench and the KMS PoC. I'll set up follow-up. Thanks everyone.

Recap and next steps discussed.

Transcript notes: There's occasional transcription noise: 'dedicated' sometimes transcribed as 'dedicate', 'control plane' misspells as 'ctrl plane', and 'KV cache' as 'kay vee cache'.

End of transcript.
